m01: The outlined pink names, for example ".abarth" and ".adac" in the first row and ".大众汽车" or ".테스트" in the non-Latin rows, render as fuzzy, faint shapes. Use a fill or underline that keeps the small text crisp.

In the Arabic rows, for example the line that ends at the left margin with "امارات.", the leading dots fall at the wrong end of each name, and bold and regular weights alternate unpredictably. Isolate each RTL name so it reads as one unit.

In the footer, the two-line caption on the right does not line up with the "Not Assigned" title on the left, and its second line in red is ragged against the first. Align the caption's first baseline with the title and let it wrap as one paragraph.
m02: In the last six rows above the footer, the names are struck through in pale grey. They are close to unreadable, especially where the strike line crosses the Arabic and CJK names on the final row, so they need a darker tone or a marking that does not cover the letters.

The small-caps group labels such as "AMAZON REGISTRY SERVICES 50" and "DOG BEACH 48" sit in the middle of a running line. Start each group on its own line so the reader can see where one registry ends and the next begins.

The label "NOT ASSIGNED 158" sits at the far right end of the line that starts ".voting .sc .name", and its names begin on the line below. Move the label to the start of the struck-through block so it sits next to the names it introduces.
m03: Some names are set in italic, such as ".coop", ".arpa", ".asia", ".int" and ".xxx", but the footer key explains only bold and the boxes. Explain the italic or drop it.
The boxed names are pale pink text inside a pale pink frame, which is hard to read. This is worst for the non-Latin ones near the bottom, such as ".テスト" and ".珠宝". Darken the boxed text.
The last line of the text block holds only ".zuerich .zw", stranded at the left above the rule. Rebalance the lines so the block does not end on a two-word orphan.
m04: The footer caption that starts "All 1595 top-level domains..." runs off the right edge and is cut mid-word after "or kept". Wrap it within the margin.
The grey "every other name" text, for example ".aaa .aarp" in the first row, is too dark against the near-black background to read comfortably. Raise its lightness.

In the legend under "NOT ASSIGNED", the "country code" and "every other name" swatches are two greys you can hardly tell apart. In the text, the country codes such as ".ac" are likewise only slightly brighter than their neighbours, so increase that difference.
m05: The horizontal rule under the text block runs right through the last line of names (".xperia .xxx .xyz .yachts ... .zw"), cutting their descenders. Move the rule down so it clears the text.

The hollow names such as ".afamilycompany" at the end of the first row and ".bentley" or ".bananarepublic" further down are pale outlines that almost vanish against the background. Give them more contrast.

Several registry colours are too close to tell apart in small text, for example the red of Binky Moon, the magenta of Identity Digital and the purple of Registry Services (compare ".archi" with ".casa" in row three). Choose hues that are further apart.
m06: In the footer legend at bottom right, the sample "158 delegated to no one" is itself struck through in red, so its number is hard to read. Show a struck sample word next to plain legend text instead.
The final line of names (". 新 加 坡  فلسطين.  . テ ス ト  . 政 务") has been stretched by justification, so spaces open up between the CJK characters. Set the last line flush left without stretching.

The faint grey tier, for example ".academy" and ".accountants" in the first row, is too light against the cream background to read at this size. Darken it so it stays clearly lighter than the bold names but can still be read.
m07: The background names are such a faint grey, for example ".aaa .aarp" at top left, that the full root reads as fog and the order around each dark name is lost. Raise their contrast a little.
The last line of names (". 新 加 坡  فلسطين.  . テ ス ト  . 政 务") is stretched by justification, so wide gaps open between the CJK characters. Leave the final line unjustified.

The footer caption at bottom right ("158 of 1,595 top-level domains ... 2026-10-09") is small pale grey, crammed against the right margin, and sits on a different baseline from the large "Not assigned" title. Align the two and darken the caption.
m08: The country codes in black (such as ".ac" and ".ad" in the first row) are barely darker than the grey "someone else" names around them. Make the country tier noticeably heavier or darker so the legend's black square matches something you can see.

In the footer legend at bottom right, the swatch for "158 given back, no one" is a pale grey square that almost disappears. Darken the swatch, or show a struck sample word, so it matches the struck names in the text.
The legend sits far to the right on the same line as "Tenancy" and starts with a long sentence, so the colour key is hard to find. Put the swatches on their own row, closer to the title.
m09: The struck-through names are light grey with a grey line through them, for example ".abarth" in the first row and ".volkswagen" near the bottom, which makes them nearly invisible. Give them more contrast or use a mark that leaves the letters legible.

In the Arabic rows near the bottom, for example the line that starts "السعودية .پارت .سودان", the monospace font falls back to a different face. The leading dots also land on the wrong side of the names, so the rows look broken. Isolate each RTL name so its dot stays with it.

The footer legend after "Vacant Lots" runs almost to the right margin and ends in "delegated to no one 158" in pale grey strikethrough, which is the hardest item to read. Make that legend sample darker and give the line some breathing room.
m10: The 158 unassigned names are replaced by pale grey blocks with no text, for example right after ".aarp" in the first row, so the reader cannot tell which names they are. Keep the name visible inside the shaded block.

In the Arabic rows near the bottom, for example the red line starting ". الاردن . پاکستان", the monospace setting pulls the Arabic letters apart into a spaced, disjointed form. Use a proportional font with Arabic support for those names.
The last row of the text block holds only ".zm .zone .zuerich .zw", which leaves a short orphan line before the footer. Rebalance the line breaks.
m11: The marked names are light grey italic on a beige fill, for example ".abarth" and ".aigo" in the first two rows, so the items the piece is about are the hardest to read. Darken their text.
The footer caption next to "Vacancies in the Root" is small and pale grey and runs nearly the full width. Darken it and shorten the line length so it can be read.
In the Arabic row near the bottom-left that reads "المغرب. بهارت. بارت.", the dots trail at the wrong end of each name. Isolate each RTL name so its leading dot stays attached.
m12: The text block ends with ".zw" alone on the last line at the left, followed by a large empty gap before the footer rule. Rebalance the final lines and tighten the space above the rule.

The header's red sentence at top right, "158 of them listed with no one to manage them", repeats "them" awkwardly. The footer key "Shaded: manager listed as 'Not assigned'" says the same thing again in pale grey, so merge the two into one clear key.

In the Arabic row that starts at the left with "ايران .العليان .اتصالات", the RTL names reorder across the line, and the shaded ".اتصالات" has its dot on the wrong side. Isolate each RTL name so the order and dots stay intact.
